answer: Each identity locks 60 credits in a vault and posts a verifiable-delay proof: a seeded 30-minute sequential computation, unsplittable. It opens with the identity's own relic, its sealed last-epoch output; a fake with none pays 40 credits to mint one. One machine is one island: a rented island shares fingerprints and freezes. Each fake costs 100 credits, so 1,000 fakes cost 100,000 credits; an honest agent pays 60 once, keeping its full share.
